bottom_line: Acetazolamide (500 mg once daily) added to intravenous loop diuretics increased successful decongestion within 3 days versus placebo (risk ratio, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.17 to 1.82).
implications: In this trial of 519 randomized patients with acute decompensated heart failure and clinical volume overload, adding acetazolamide to standardized intravenous loop diuretics increased the incidence of successful decongestion within 3 days (42.2% vs. 30.5%; risk ratio, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.17 to 1.82). The trial does not show a difference in the 3-month composite of death from any cause or rehospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.48), and reported prespecified safety events during the treatment phase were similar between groups (e.g., hypokalemia 5.5% vs 3.9%; hypotension 6.6% vs 3.5%).

major_points.text: Multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in acute decompensated heart failure with volume overload.
major_points.quote: In this multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, we assigned patients with acute decompensated heart failure, clinical signs of volume overload

major_points.text: Randomized acetazolamide 500 mg IV once daily vs matching placebo added to standardized IV loop diuretics at twice the oral maintenance dose.
major_points.quote: to receive either intra- venous acetazolamide (500 mg once daily) or placebo added to standardized intra- venous loop diuretics (at a dose equivalent to twice the oral maintenance dose).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was successful decongestion within 3 days without indication for escalation of decongestive therapy.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was successful decongestion, defined as the absence of signs of volume overload, within 3 days after randomization and without an indication for escalation of decongestive therapy.

major_points.text: Successful decongestion occurred more often with acetazolamide than placebo.
major_points.quote: Successful decongestion occurred in 108 of 256 patients (42.2%) in the acetazolamide group and in 79 of 259 (30.5%) in the placebo group (risk ratio, 1.46; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.17 to 1.82;

major_points.text: Composite of death from any cause or rehospitalization for heart failure during 3 months did not differ significantly between groups.
major_points.quote: Death from any cause or rehospitalization for heart failure occurred in 76 of 256 patients (29.7%) in the acetazolamide group and in 72 of 259 patients (27.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.48).

major_points.text: Incidence of worsening kidney function, hypokalemia, hypotension, and adverse events was similar in the two groups.

analysis_methods.text: Targeted sample size 494; planned enrollment 519 accounting for 5% withdrawal.
analysis_methods.quote: we calculated the targeted sample size for the trial to be 494, and to account for a potential withdrawal of 5% of the patients, we calculated that the trial would need to enroll 519 patients.

analysis_methods.text: Primary and secondary endpoint analyses were intention-to-treat including randomized patients who received at least one dose; four patients excluded for receiving neither trial drug nor placebo.
analysis_methods.quote: The analyses of the primary and secondary end points were based on the intention-to-treat principle and included data from all the patients who had undergone randomization and received at least one dose of acetazolamide or placebo; four patients were excluded

analysis_methods.text: Primary endpoint analyzed using a generalized linear mixed model (log-link binomial) with fixed treatment and LVEF strata effects and random center effect.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary end point was evaluated by means of a generalized linear mixed model (log-link binomial model) that included a fixed treatment effect, a fixed effect for the stratification factor of the left ventricular ejection fraction, and a random center effect

analysis_methods.text: Death/rehospitalization composite analyzed with Cox proportional-hazards model including trial group, LVEF stratification factor, and random center effect (log-normal frailty).
analysis_methods.quote: was assessed in a time-to- event analysis with the use of a Cox proportion- al-hazards model that included trial group, the stratification factor of the left ventricular ejec- tion fraction, and a random center effect (with the use of a log-normal frailty model)

analysis_methods.text: No multiplicity correction was prespecified for secondary or other outcomes; confidence intervals not adjusted.
analysis_methods.quote: the statistical analysis plan did not include a provision for correction for multi- plicity when tests for secondary or other outcomes were conducted

analysis_methods.text: Safety events compared using Fisher’s exact test.

criticisms.text: Nearly all participants were White and recruitment was exclusively in Belgium, which may limit generalizability to other racial or ethnic groups.
criticisms.quote: Nearly all the patients who participated in the trial were White, given that the trial recruited exclusively in Belgium, which may limit the generalizability of our re- sults to other racial or ethnic groups.

criticisms.text: Participants had chronic heart failure and long-term outpatient loop diuretic treatment; results may not apply to newly diagnosed heart failure.
criticisms.quote: patients also had a history of chronic heart fail- ure and had been receiving long-term outpatient treatment with at least 40 mg of furosemide equivalent. Therefore, results of the strategy we tested may not be applicable to patients with newly diagnosed heart failure.

criticisms.text: Unclear whether similar results would be obtained with other loop-diuretic dosing regimens or other diuretic agents.
criticisms.quote: It is unknown whether simi- lar results may have been obtained with other dose regimens of loop diuretics or other diuretic agents.

criticisms.text: SGLT2 inhibitors were excluded, so results are in a setting avoiding imbalance in their use between groups.
criticisms.quote: To avoid confound- ing by any imbalance in their use between the trial groups, the trial design excluded their use.
